blurb: A suite helper that returns an `Effect` must say which capabilities it uses, with `given`, so a case's dependency on it is visible where it is called: `fn seed() -> Effect[()] given Stock { … }`. Without `given` it is a pure function that builds a value for a case, so build the value in the helper and run the effect in the `case`, where each step is visible with `<-`.
example:
// tests/desk.test.bynk
fn bump(n: Int) -> Effect[Int] { local.call(n) }   // ✗ returns an `Effect`, with no `given`
fn start() -> Int { 1 }                            // ✓ build the value
let n <- local.call(start())                       // ✓ run it in the case
summary: A suite helper `fn` returns an `Effect`; suite helpers are pure.
